constraints: Memory is Model Plane (session-core/execution-core); Data Plane v2 has no agent-derived write path today, so the item's 'Data Plane enforces the same flag' clause has nothing to enforce. ZDR already prevents durable memory writes and Dreaming never sees ZDR turns, so the guard only concerns persistent runs; a quarantine must also stop the Letta semantic mirror because Letta reads in memory_grpc search/list are not filtered by review_state. Taint must be thread-window level, not only run level: Dreaming extracts from a window that includes up to 6 earlier consolidated messages and assistant turns that paraphrase web content. Only the memory owner may promote a quarantined memory and Space membership must not widen that.
approachAdjustment: Do not use the ZDR credential flag as the carrier: MemoryRetention is derived from the token fixed at issuance, while taint appears mid-run. (1) In execution-core, save_memory preflight marks or refuses the write when the run's own tool history contains web_search/web_fetch/web.*/browser.*/mcp__* calls (data_category already distinguishes them). (2) In session-core Dreaming, skip or write 'pending' for extraction windows whose thread has such tool steps, derived from session_tool_audit_intents/step records, and suppress the Letta mirror for them. (3) Ship skip-only first with no promotion UI; add the pending-review path later through the memory management surface. Remove the Data Plane and graph clauses until an agent-derived graph write path exists.
effortNote: Item said S. S holds for a skip-only first slice (execution-core preflight plus a Dreaming window filter); the pending-review path needs a new accept/reject RPC (none exists in memory.proto or memory_grpc.rs), Letta mirror suppression and a UI, which is M.
verdictReason: The guard is genuinely absent and worth building, but the carrier (credential-bound ZDR pattern), the Data Plane clause and the S estimate are wrong; reword to the thread-level taint approach with a skip-only first slice. Existing prompt-level and provenance mitigations should be mentioned so the document does not say memory is entirely unprotected.

constraints: Space authority: a stored schedule is never authority, every create needs a Control decision bound to the user and every fire is reauthorized, so an agent-created routine must go through the same user-bound create decision, never a service insert. The scheduled lane must not borrow a human's delegated bearer, which conflicts with the item's 'fresh BrowserBroker grant per fire' because browser tools need a delegated browser credential and the broker has no issuance path. Owner ruling: unattended runs are draft-only through Wave 2 and effectful or browser tool use in scheduled runs is Wave-3 scope, needing a pause/resume path that does not exist. ZDR: the scheduled lane is hard-wired persistent, so 'ZDR routines persist no transcript' cannot hold; refuse routine creation for ZDR users or build a non-persistent lane. Model proposes, Quarry executes: browser steps in a routine still need the Quarry grant and per-action approvals, which cannot be answered unattended.
approachAdjustment: Re-scope in stages. (1) An agent-proposed routine as a confirmed, user-bound schedule create (the tool returns a proposal the user approves, then the existing gateway create_cron path runs), draft-only and tool-free. (2) Event triggers by adding Watch adapters or generalizing mail-task, not by building a new matcher. (3) Tool-using or browser routines only after the Wave-3 approval pause/resume design, a scoped service-owned browser credential and BrowserBroker issuance exist. Keep acquisition-only automation (watch a page) on Quarry schedules (ingestions.create_schedule) rather than agent routines.
effortNote: L sized this as an extension of cron_schedules, but per-fire browser grants and tool-using routines need a scheduled tool loop, approval pause/resume, a scoped service browser credential and a ZDR lane. The draft-only agent-proposed routine alone is M.
verdictReason: The cron foundation exists, but the distinctive parts (heartbeat, event routines, per-fire browser grants) are blocked by the Wave-3 draft-only ruling and unbuilt prerequisites (grant issuance, scheduled tool loop, ZDR lane). Keep as a later-wave item with the narrowed first slice.

constraints: Plane ownership: grants belong to the Model Plane (browser-broker, Go with no database today, so durable storage adds a datastore dependency); Quarry only validates. No cross-plane DB access: Quarry must publish AuthzDecision over NATS and never write audit-core tables, and because Quarry has no audit publisher one must be added with its own plane/producer/event subject family and publish grant (audit-core rejects an event whose subject tokens do not match the payload). Privacy and ZDR: events carry origin only and ZDR tags, never full URLs, and per-navigation validations should be recorded denials-only. Space authority: child-run and fleet grants may only narrow (min of parent scopes) and never inherit wider authority through a Space. The webhook org_id migration must handle existing unscoped rows fail-closed.
approachAdjustment: Split into three independently shippable items. (a) Durable, issued BrowserBroker grants, merged with F-t2-001 rather than treating persistence and issuance separately, with parent/child inheritance on the existing parent_grant_id binding. (b) Quarry webhook tenant scoping: org_id column with migration, edge-fronted org-scoped CRUD, dispatch-id header. (c) AuthzDecision audit as a new event name on the existing verevon.audit.v2 flat shape, first published by session-core/execution-core approval decisions with decided_by filled from the durable record, and only later by Quarry policy denials. Demote the evaluate/raw-CSS sensitive-allowlist change to low-priority hardening because both facades already refuse those actions.
effortNote: As one item this bundles a new broker datastore plus issuance path, a Quarry webhook migration and edge exposure, and a cross-plane audit event with a new Quarry publisher. Split, it is roughly M (webhooks), M (audit) and L (durable grants plus issuance, overlapping F-t2-001).
